terms.meaning: The framework that builds and serves this web app.
A shell that wraps every page with the parts they all share.
A setting supplied to the app from outside its code, such as a site address.
The moment the browser attaches interactivity to a page that the server already drew.
The visible area of the screen on a device.
A small file that describes the app so a phone can install it like an app.

used_by: Every page under src/app. Next.js applies this root layout automatically, and those pages are not listed in this packet.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Shared imports
sections.what: Loads the three font families, the global stylesheet, the sign-in wrapper, the app shell, the offline app registration, and the theme colour values.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are loaded once here so every page gets them.
sections.watch_out: Removing any one of these imports changes the look or behaviour of every page at once.

sections.name: metadata
sections.title: Page title and site address
sections.what: Sets the browser tab title pattern, so the app name appears alone or after a page name. It also sets the description used by search and link previews, the app manifest link, the home-screen app settings, and the site address used when building links.
sections.why: The code comment explains the address fallback: an empty environment variable must fall back to a default, because an invalid address stops the build.
sections.watch_out: If the site address environment variable is not set in production, links and previews will point to localhost.

sections.name: viewport
sections.title: Phone screen settings
sections.what: Tells phones to use the full device width, keeps zoom enabled, and sets the top bar colour for light and dark modes so the phone status bar matches.
sections.why: The code comment says zoom was blocked before and that blocking it fails accessibility guidelines.
sections.watch_out: Do not block zooming again, since the comment records it as an accessibility failure.

sections.name: RootLayout
sections.title: Page frame and theme script
sections.what: Builds the HTML frame in English. A small script in the head applies the saved light or dark theme before the page first draws, falling back to the device setting. It also links the touch and home-screen icons, then places the page content inside the sign-in wrapper, the app shell, and the offline app registration.
sections.why: The code comment says the theme is set before the first paint, so the page does not flash the wrong colours. Likely reason for the hydration warning setting: the script changes the page before React checks it.
sections.watch_out: The theme script reads the saved theme from browser storage under the key ae_theme, so renaming that key would silently stop saved themes from applying.

summary: Root layout that wraps every page with fonts, global styles, sign-in state, the app shell, and offline app support.
purpose: Holds the shared frame and page tags for the whole app.
why: It is loaded once so that every page shares the same fonts, sign-in state, and layout.
how: Steps in order: it loads fonts and global styles, sets the page title pattern, description, and site address, sets the phone viewport and theme colours, then renders the HTML frame. The frame includes a small theme script that runs before the page draws, icon links, and the shared wrappers around the page content.
inputs: The page content that Next.js passes in, the site address environment variable, the theme saved in the browser under a specific storage key, and the theme colour settings.
outputs: The full HTML frame for every page in the app.
risks: A broken import here breaks every page at once. An unset site address makes link previews point to localhost. A broken theme script causes a colour flash on load.
debug: If every page fails, check the imports and the wrapper components first. If link previews or shared links are wrong, check the site address environment variable. If the theme is wrong on load, check the saved theme value in the browser and the theme script.
